subject.title: exec auto-reviewer re-bills a fresh model completion for every byte-identical repeated exec

question: May OpenClaw reuse model-backed exec reviewer decisions for byte-identical requests within one reviewer/run, and what fields and lifetime must define that cache key?
rationale: The repeated cost is real, but caching an exec approval reviewer result changes the approval security boundary by letting a later request skip a fresh model review.

options.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
options.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt, without persisting or converting them to durable approval.

options.title: Memoize allow-once only
options.body: Cache only low-risk allow-once results and keep ask, error, and timeout decisions uncached for a narrower but less complete cost fix.

options.title: Keep fresh review semantics
options.body: Accept repeated reviewer completions for identical commands until stronger security or live billing evidence justifies approval-result reuse.

recommendation.title: Approve full-input per-run memo
recommendation.body: Cache parsed reviewer decisions only inside the shared reviewer instance, keyed by the full reviewed input or prompt, without persisting or converting them to durable approval.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle is tied to the introducing normalized auto mode PR and later trusted reviewer policy work, so it is the strongest available owner for the cache-scope decision.
